items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I knew Al many years before, having met him and Sy (Melvin) Oliver in Zanesville, Ohio, when I played that town with the Scott band before we went to New-York.

ctx.x: Dick and I were in the White Rose after every intermission. They had a free snack table in this bar which at one time there were a few hot dishes to choose from, but people started to abuse the hospitality and now there were only cold cuts, cheese and crackers. Of course you had to buy a drink or drinks to ride this gravy train. Dick and I paid our dues every night.

Shortly before we finished at the Door, Dick became ill and was taken to the Harlem Hospital. No one thought that his sickness was very serious and all agreed that the rest would be good for him. Al Sears was engaged to sub for Dick and he had a style that suited the band. I knew Al many years before, having met him and Sy (Melvin) Oliver in Zanesville, Ohio, when I played that town with the Scott band before we went to New-York.

After the famous Door gig, the band hit the road which was customary for the Kirk band and the first date was at an amusement park for one night in Montreal, Canada. It was considered a usual habit for the band to make a jump of 500 or more miles from one place to another in a bus and play only one night. I had done plenty of one nighters with Clarence Page, Wes Helvey and Scott, but they were seldom over a couple of hundred miles.
